posts.title: Missing classes for neu london scholars
posts.content: so they told us that skipping classes and getting bellow i think 70% attendance means that your visa will be removed. I am currently kinda sick but am too scared to miss classes. Have anyone else had experience with missing classes as a london cholar? they say to put evidence in the seats app but what do i put for a mild cough and cold? also if i miss a class what happens? do i get a notification or what?

comments.body: Was at London last year, do not worry. You can miss 2 classes a week and your attendance will still be 75% for the week. If you have below 70% for 2 weeks IN A ROW then you will get a warning and then if u have 4 weeks in A ROW then you will get another warning and a meeting, and then 6 weeks in a row is another meeting and the last warning and then 8 weeks IN A ROW is visa removal. So basically you can miss 2 classes a week for the whole year and nothing will happen. Basically impossible to get your visa revoked unless you miss 3 classes a week for 8 weeks. Just stick to missing 2 a week and maybe you can skip 3 one week and then only miss 1 class the next week and you will be at 70%

posts.title: Does co-op actually make Northeastern affordable for international student ?
posts.content:
Hi everyone,



I’m an international student looking at Northeastern for MS in Computer Science , and the co-op program is a big part of why it’s on my list. I’d really like to hear from people who have been through it, especially other international students.



From the outside, co-op looks like a great way to gain real work experience while offsetting the cost of tuition, but I want to understand how it plays out in practice. A few things I’m curious about:



How much of your tuition did co-op earnings realistically cover? Did it make a noticeable difference, or was it more of a “helps with living expenses” situation?

How hard was it to land a paid co-op as an international student? Did visa/CPT constraints limit your options?

Were there any hidden costs or surprises (tuition during co-op semesters, fees, relocation, timing issues, etc.)?

Was the co-op pay enough to live on, especially in expensive cities like Boston or the Bay Area?

Would you still choose Northeastern for the co-op if you were making the decision again, given the total cost?



I’m not looking for a sales pitch in either direction. Honest experiences, good or bad, would help a lot. If you’re willing to share rough numbers or your timeline, even better.



Thanks in advance!

comments.body: Nothing is affordable about studying in northeastern without a grant/scholarship as an international student. Coop makes some money sure but you’re at a temporary entry level position.
comments.author: Gon_Snow

comments.body:
I agree with this. Are you trying to compare it with some other school in particular? Depends on that too.

Also, getting a coop in this market (especially for international students) is not as easy as the stats make it sound.

I wouldn’t count on getting a coop as a way to make Northeastern affordable tbh because it’s not guaranteed given the market and other factors.

Good luck!
comments.author: Dependent-Judge-2657

comments.body:
Fair point, it’s hard to call Northeastern affordable for internationals without funding.

On conversion, Northeastern says more than half of graduates get a full-time offer from a co-op employer. One guide puts it at 52% for master’s students. But these are university numbers and don’t separate international students, whose odds are probably lower because of sponsorship.

Do you know how it went for internationals? Did your co-op employer offer a return role and sponsor?

comments.body: Yes many pay off an entire semesters fees with the coop earnings

posts.title: NEU students: what was your last UHCS visit actually like? (student project, not a complaint thread)
posts.content:
**Quick survey: your honest UHCS experiences (for a class project)**

Hey all,a few of us are working on a project looking at University Health and Counseling Services and want real student experiences, not just what's on the website. No wrong answers, and feel free to be blunt.

If you've used UHCS (medical or mental health side), we'd love to hear:

* What was the actual process like, booking, triage call, walk-in, whatever applied to you?
* What was the most frustrating part, if any?
* Was there anything that worked *well* that surprised you?
* Anything that happened outside normal hours (evenings, weekends) what did you do?
* If you have an international/visa status, any experience with medical documentation (RCL, leave of absence, etc.)?
* Anything about communication like follow-ups, getting results, knowing what to do next?

Totally fine to DM instead of commenting if you'd rather keep it private. Thanks!
